title: Make Pi's advisory gaps enforced by name instead of by prose
action: Nothing today forces a Pi advisory gap to be named: the Pi suite's advisory assertion is a hand-written expected list checked with contains, which can never catch a NEW catalog rule the belt fails to wire. OpenCode already has the gate this needs — a test that derives the rule catalog from the checked-in manifests and fails when a rule is neither wired nor named as an exclusion. Generalize that existing test over both belts rather than writing a second one in the Pi suite: read the cited coverage-gate pattern first, then note that the OpenCode test file already holds the catalog derivation, the embedded Pi belt source and the Pi naming predicate, while the Pi suite file embeds no manifest at all — building the gate there would mean deriving the same catalog twice. Add the Pi-side advisory-hook derivation beside the OpenCode one and run the same gap loop for both belts. Expect the gate to be RED the moment you write it, and treat that red as the point: only one rule in the belt currently carries the exclusion marker on its own line, while the others are described in prose without it, so the predicate returns false for them. Fix that by rewording those belt comments so each excluded rule's name and the marker sit on the SAME line — the predicate is line-scoped on purpose, so a marker on a neighbouring line does not count. Do not weaken the predicate to make the red go away. Keep every existing exclusion reason intact; you are moving words onto one line, not changing what is excluded or why.

truths: A catalog advisory rule that the Pi belt neither wires nor names on one line fails the gate
The gate derives its ground truth once, from the manifests, and does not introduce a second catalog derivation
Every rule the Pi belt deliberately does not wire carries its name and the exclusion marker on the same line
No exclusion reason is changed or dropped — only reformatted onto one line
The gate is red before the belt comments are fixed and green after, and the cap records both observations
